notes: Transaction is supported by a PO, two invoice scans, a bank statement, and a ledger entry, but several unresolved issues limit confidence. (1) INV-1009-A and INV-1009-B are identical duplicate scans of the same supplier invoice (PIS/2026/091, same date/amount) - this raises a double-billing/duplicate-submission risk; only one payment (BNK-1009) matches the invoiced amount, so no double payment is evidenced, but the duplicate document itself is unresolved. (2) The invoiced/paid/ledgered amount (INR 141,600.00) exceeds PO-1009's authorized total (INR 118,000.00) by INR 23,600.00 - internal consistency among invoice, bank statement, and ledger does not resolve this discrepancy against the PO, which remains a possible pricing/overbilling issue requiring explanation (e.g., a change order or PO amendment, none of which is present). (3) No goods receipt or delivery confirmation document is present in this case to independently verify that goods/services matching the PO and invoiced amount were actually received; the successful bank payment does not substitute for this. (4) The ledger entry corroborates the payment but cannot break out tax separately, so tax reconciliation relies solely on the invoice figures, which themselves are the duplicated/discrepant documents.
